summary:
I worked all 7 original results items under RBC-INBOX-01. Four more arrived while I worked: I acted on three, and one has to stay open (pt-0007 chest X-ray, below). Two of the new arrivals changed decisions I had already made, so I corrected those orders and messages and wrote down why.

**Still open / needs you:**
- **pt-0007 Leslie Parisian, chest X-ray 10-22 (inbox-a0002):** left open on purpose. The only report is a preliminary read: "possible 7 mm right upper lobe nodule; consider CT." Policy says to act only on the final report, and none has been issued yet.
- **I can't cancel lab or imaging orders with my tools, so two superseded orders are still active.** I made a task to discontinue each:
  - task-t0022: urgent BMP sr-t0014 for pt-0008, now replaced by the stat BMP.
  - task-t0030: 12-month low-dose CT sr-t0001 and its tracking task task-t0002 for pt-0006, now replaced by the 6-month scan.
- **Medication questions I flagged in the notes but didn't change (outside these policies):**
  - pt-0007 has an active naproxen prescription (as needed, with clopidogrel) and now has acute kidney injury.
  - pt-0033 is on hydrochlorothiazide and insulin 70/30 and now has acute kidney injury.

**pt-0008 Walter Brennan, potassium 6.4:**
- At first the result was flagged hemolyzed (possibly falsely high). I ordered an urgent repeat BMP and messaged him to come in, without notifying on-call, as the hemolysis rule says.
- At 07:55 the lab corrected it: the hemolysis comment belonged to another patient's sample, and the 6.4 stands.
- I switched to the critical-potassium rule:
  - on-call was messaged at stat priority and asked to phone him today
  - stat BMP ordered for today (sr-t0018)
  - a correction went to him telling him to come in today
- None of his medications raise potassium, so there was nothing to hold. Note written; item closed.

**pt-0006 Raj Patel, CT urogram 10-19:**
- The CT found no cause for the blood in his urine. It also showed a 4 mm left lower lobe lung nodule that is already followed in his lung cancer screening.
- I first ordered his next screening low-dose CT for March 14 – May 14, 2027, with a tracking task, a message to him and a note.
- Then Lakeshore faxed an addendum to his April 14 screening CT: a new 5 mm right upper lobe nodule, rated "probably benign" (Lung-RADS 3), with a repeat CT recommended in 6 months.
- That window runs Sept 14 – Nov 14, 2026 and is still open. I ordered the scan for Oct 23 – Nov 14 (sr-t0028), with a tracking task due Nov 14 and a corrected message to him. Note written; both items closed.

**pt-0007 Leslie Parisian:**
- **BMP 10-22:** creatinine 1.64 versus 0.98 35 hours earlier, which meets the acute kidney injury rule. I ordered an urgent repeat BMP by Mon 10-26, messaged him today (including advice to avoid NSAIDs) and wrote a note. Item closed.
- **Chest CT angiogram:** the preliminary read mentioned a nodule, but the final report says no blood clot and no nodule (it was a blood vessel) and needs no follow-up imaging. Closed with that comment, and he was told in the same message.

**pt-0033 Carol Whitfield, creatinine:**
- The 10-22 morning value of 1.31 did not meet the acute kidney injury rule. The 0.84 on 10-21 was entered in error (another patient's sample), so I didn't compare against it. I closed that item with no action.
- An urgent care creatinine of 1.78 from that evening then arrived: a rise of 0.47 in 9 hours, which does meet the rule. I ordered an urgent repeat BMP by 10-26, messaged her and wrote a note explaining the changed decision. Item closed.

**pt-0016 Edra Ondricka:** TSH was normal. The potassium was corrected from 6.3 (an analyzer fault) to a normal 4.4. Both were acknowledged and closed with no action.

evidence.quote: The lab has told us that your October 22 blood sample was NOT damaged after all, so your high potassium result (6.4 mmol/L) is likely real.
Revised impression Lung-RADS 3; revised recommendation LDCT in 6 months.
